title: AML/CFT Guideline amended: ongoing monitoring and PEP scope
summary: Chapter 4 is amended to require continuous rather than periodic monitoring for higher-risk relationships, and widens the definition of a politically exposed person to include domestic PEPs and their close associates.

diff.text: An authorised institution should continuously monitor its business relationship with a customer,
review existing records periodically to ensure documents remain up to date
review existing records on a continuous and event-driven basis to ensure documents, data and information remain up to date and relevant
and scrutinise complex or unusually large transactions.
For the purposes of this Chapter, a politically exposed person includes a domestic politically exposed person and their close associates.

title: Draft direction on digital lending partnerships
summary: Extends the key fact statement requirement to loans sourced through lending service providers and requires the all-inclusive annual percentage rate to be shown before the borrower consents.

diff.text: Regulated entities shall provide a key fact statement to the borrower before execution of the contract,
including where the loan is sourced or serviced through a lending service provider,
disclose the all-inclusive annual percentage rate,

title: DORA incident reporting templates finalised
summary: The harmonised templates are final. The intermediate report window shortens from 72 to 48 hours and a new field set is required for third-party-originated incidents.

diff.text: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the competent authority using harmonised templates,
submitting an intermediate report within 72 hours
submitting an intermediate report within 48 hours, and identifying whether the incident originated with a third-party provider

title: Consumer Duty board report expectations clarified
summary: The annual board report must now evidence outcomes for customers in vulnerable circumstances separately, with supporting data.

diff.text: A firm must act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers
and must evidence, separately, outcomes for customers in vulnerable circumstances in its annual board report.

title: Regulation B record retention period under review
summary: A proposal would extend the retention window for business-credit applications from 12 to 25 months, aligning it with consumer credit.

diff.text: (12 months for business credit, except as provided in paragraph (b)(5) of this section)
after the date that a creditor notifies an applicant of action taken on an application
